title: MINOR: Drain buffered bytes before continuing delegated skips
body:
When delegated `skip` returns zero, `ChunkedBytesStream.skip` reads through its own buffered `read()` method. That can fill the intermediate buffer, after which subsequent delegated skips move the source past unread buffered bytes. With input bytes 0–9 and a four-byte buffer, a source whose first skip returns zero makes `skip(5)` report success while the next read returns 1 instead of 5.

Consume any bytes prefetched by the fallback read before delegating another skip. This preserves the existing buffered codec path. The regression tests verify the full remaining sequence for skips within the buffer, beyond the buffer, and through EOF, plus repeated skips through real LZ4 frames containing consecutive empty compressed blocks.

Validation: compiled the actual production classes and the full `ChunkedBytesStreamTest` class with `javac --release 11` on JDK 21, then ran JUnit Jupiter 5.14.4 and Mockito 5.23.0. The unchanged production code fails 2 of 56 tests; the fix passes all 56. The three real LZ4 boundary cases also pass. File-scoped checks using Kafka's Checkstyle 12.3.1 configuration and Spotless 4.10.0 import-order step pass.

The LZ4 checks compile the current decoder and helper sources; a cached Kafka clients 3.9.2 jar supplies auxiliary compile-time signatures. They do not validate the complete current clients module or record batches. The official Gradle tasks, full clients suite, and CI JDKs 17/25 have not been run locally.
